decontamination_notes: Real host-injection input-validation fix from urllib3/urllib3 PR #5095 ('Reject invalid URL hosts'), merged 2026-06-30 -- after the training cutoffs of the models evaluated here (e.g. Opus 5, May 2026), so the specific fix is not in their training data (decontaminated: true), with upstream_merged recorded as proof. parse_url() did not validate the host component, so a URL whose authority contained a control character (CR/LF/NUL/space) -- literally or percent-encoded -- parsed into a Url with that character in .host. Downstream this enables Host-header / CRLF injection, request splitting/smuggling, and SSRF-style host confusion. The fix (src/urllib3/util/url.py, parse_url + _normalize_host) rejects any host containing a control char or space via a new invalid-char regex, changes the host/port match to a fullmatch, and rejects percent-encoded control octets, raising LocationParseError. urllib3 has no runtime dependencies; the sliced src/ tree keeps a realistic navigation surface, but the package __init__ files were emptied because the real ones import a build-time-generated urllib3/_version.py (absent from source) -- the fix and tests only need urllib3.util.url + urllib3.exceptions, imported offline with PYTHONPATH=src on the base image (Python 3.12). Repo sliced at the PR base commit (12k LOC; parse_url still accepting control chars in the host); MIT LICENSE preserved. Coverage floor: 3 fail_to_pass (a raw newline, a raw carriage return, and a percent-encoded NUL in the host are each accepted at base and raise LocationParseError after the fix) plus a 2-check regression guard (an ordinary domain and an IPv4 literal still parse).
